Lakshya Sen vs Koki Watanabe, Japan Masters 2026 FINAL LIVE SCORE — Indian shuttler eyes title in Kumamoto
 Lakshya Sen vs Koki Watanabe LIVE — Follow the score, updates and highlights of the Japan Masters 2026 men's singles final, being played in Kumamoto, Japan.
 Updated : Nov 15, 2026 08:56 IST

 Shiv Kumar Pushpakar
 W elcome to Sportstar’s live coverage of the Japan Masters 2026 men’s singles final, between Lakshya Sen from India and Koki Watanabe from Japan, being played at the Kumamoto Prefectural Gymnasium (also referred to as the Kumamoto Prefectural General Gymnasium) in Kumamoto, Japan.
 November 15, 2026 08:56 
 Lakshya into double digits
 After a brilliant 47-shot rally, Laksya’s cross-court shot earns him a point as he goes to double digits and adds another to reach 11-12. Watanabe then goes for a smash to go 13-11 up.
 November 15, 2026 08:54 
 Lakshya eyes comeback
 Lakshya checks Watanabe’s footing as he runs back and thinks the shuttlecock is going out. But it’s not. Lakshya gets a point and then goes a smash and cuts the deficit to just three points.
 The score 12-9 to Watanabe.
 November 15, 2026 08:52 
 Watanabe leads at the break
 Watanabe is tested around the corner. Lakshya ends up shooting outside the court, and then gets a point with a cross-court smash. Watanabe gets back to take a five-point advantage into the break. 
 November 15, 2026 08:49 
 Watanabe riding high on home support
 Lakshya shoots outside the court after a long rally and then Watanabe forces two more errors by the Indian shuttler to get to 7-1. Watanabe then shoots outside the court and another error from him brings the score to 7-3.
 November 15, 2026 08:47 
 Lakshya gets his first point
 Watanabe’s back hand tests Lakshya across the court and then the Indian goes for a smash to get his first point. Watanabe chooses the same option for his fourth point,
 The score: 4-1 to Watanabe.
 November 15, 2026 08:45 
 Match begins!
 Watanabe takes two early points with lightning quick reflexes, as Lakshya fails to get a touch on his return. 
 November 15, 2026 08:43 
 Players warm up before the summit clash
 A few rallies, soft backhands are exchanged between the two players before they get into the groove for the final.
 November 15, 2026 08:40 
 Players arrive on the court
 Lakshya is the first one to arrive on the court. He comes in wearing orange and with an escort kid. Koki Watanabe, the local hero, then arrives in blue.
 November 15, 2026 08:24 
 Lakshya's match slightly delayed
 The men’s singles final between Lakshya and Watanabe is slightly delayed because of the mixed doubles final has gone to the third game. 
 The pair of Jiang Zhenbang and Wei Yaxin is looking to win the title in a clash against Gao Jiaxuan and Wu Mengying in an all-China final. Jiang Zhenbang and Wei Yaxin won the contest eventually, making a comeback after losing the first game.
 November 15, 2026 08:15 
 Watanabe's route to the final
 Koki Watanabe survived tight opening games in both the Round of 16 (against Chou Tien-chen) and the Quarterfinals (against Kidambi Srikanth, where he trailed 9–14 in the second game before reeling off 10 straight points), then saved a match point in the semifinal decider to upset 2nd seed Kunlavut Vitidsarn.
 Watanabe’s route to the Japan Masters 2026 final
 Round of 32: Defeated Jeon Hyeok-jin (KOR) · 21–10, 21–18
 Round of 16: Defeated Chou Tien-chen (TPE) · 24–22, 21–19
 Quarterfinals: Defeated Kidambi Srikanth (IND) · 24–22, 21–15
 Semifinals: Defeated Kunlavut Vitidsarn (THA) [2] · 14–21, 21–11, 23–21
 November 15, 2026 08:05 
 Lakshyas’s route to Japan Masters final
 Lakshya Sen cruised through his first three rounds in straight games—extending his unbeaten streak across the Hylo Open and Kumamoto Masters to nine matches—before needing three games to dispatch 6th seed Alwi Farhan in the semifinals.
 Lakshyas’s route to Japan Masters final 
 Round of 32: Defeated Chi Yu-jen (TPE) — 21–19, 21–18
 Round of 16: Defeated Dong Tianyao (CHN) — 21–8, 21–14
 Quarterfinals: Defeated Yushi Tanaka (JPN) — 21–16, 21–15
 Semifinals: Defeated Alwi Farhan (INA) [6] — 21–12, 15–21, 21–11
 November 15, 2026 07:43 
 Lakshya Sen vs Koki Watanabe H2H:
 Lakshya Sen leads Koki Watanabe 4–3 in their career head-to-head record across seven completed meetings. 
 July 14, 2026 – Japan Open 2026 (Round of 32): Koki Watanabe defeated Lakshya Sen, 21–16, 21–14
 May 29, 2026 – Singapore Open 2026 (Quarter-finals): Koki Watanabe defeated Lakshya Sen, 21–19, 15–21, 21–15
 November 11, 2025 – Kumamoto Masters Japan 2025 (Round of 32): Lakshya Sen defeated Koki Watanabe, 21–12, 21–16
 February 16, 2024 – Badminton Asia Team Championships 2024 (Quarter-finals): Lakshya Sen defeated Koki Watanabe, 21–19, 22–20
 July 27, 2023 – Japan Open 2023 (Quarter-finals): Lakshya Sen defeated Koki Watanabe, 21–15, 21–19
 July 14, 2016 – Asia Junior Championships 2016 (U19 Round 4): Lakshya Sen defeated Koki Watanabe, 21–15, 21–18
 July 10, 2016 – Asia Junior Mixed Team Championships 2016 (Quarter-finals): Koki Watanabe defeated Lakshya Sen, 21–16, 21–11
 November 15, 2026 07:30 
 Match preview
 Lakshya Sen will look to cap another impressive week on the BWF Tour with a second consecutive title when he takes on Japan’s Koki Watanabe in the men’s singles final of the Japan Masters 2026 on Sunday.
 The Indian shuttler booked his place in the summit clash with a convincing 21-12, 15-21, 21-11 win over Indonesia’s Alwi Farhan in the semifinals on Saturday. The victory extended Lakshya’s run of form following his Hylo Open Super 500 triumph in Germany earlier this month.
 The 25-year-old, who finished runner-up at the All England Open earlier this year, will be chasing his third title-round appearance of the 2026 season. Standing in his way is home favourite Watanabe, who pulled off a major upset by defeating Paris 2024 Olympics silver medallist Kunlavut Vitidsarn in the other semifinal.
